relevance_note: Case report of one identifiable patient with LAD-I: "A 6-year-old boy diagnosed with leukocyte adhesion deficiency type I (LAD-I)".
method_note: Built by hand with a short Python script; every value from my reading. One in-scope person (rule 5 label 'patient'). No ITGB2 variant, genetic test or zygosity is reported for him (diagnosis by flow cytometry and clinical course); the only ITGB2 mention is a general statement in the Introduction, so no variant row was created. The '6-year-old' age is at referral for HSCT, not onset, diagnosis or last evaluation, so those age fields are not reported; follow-up continued 10 months to the second HSCT and 18 months after the third. Vital status 'alive' rests on the 18-month follow-up and 'favorable outcome' statements (no explicit 'alive'). The father (haploidentical donor, HLA-typed only, Table 1) is neither tested for an ITGB2 variant nor described as affected, so he gets no row. 'otitis' is unspecified, so checklist 'otitis media' is not reported; omphalitis was not used to mark 'skin or soft tissue infections'. Lower respiratory tract and fungal infection are post-second-HSCT complications (pulmonary Aspergillus infection/pneumonia) during graft failure. Post-transplant complications (graft failure, marrow hypoplasia, VOD/SOS, BK hemorrhagic cystitis, cGvHD) were recorded as observed features. Supplementary Table S1 (from ref 13) lists two previously published patients with 'LAD' (type not stated) with transplant data only; they were not given rows because LAD-I is not stated and no ITGB2 variant is given. Tables S2 and S3 contain no LAD patients. Internal inconsistencies (dosing, not phenotype): third-HSCT cyclophosphamide 25 mg/kg/day in text vs 10 mg/kg/day in Figure 1C legend; PTCY 40 vs 50 mg/kg/day; second-HSCT fludarabine 'total dose of 160 mg/kg' in text vs 30 mg/m^2/day x 5 days in Figure 1B; abstract says both failed HSCTs were 'from a matched unrelated donor'. No phenotype contradictions found.
